_comment: Edit this file to update prediction statuses without touching component code.

predictions.note: Baseline: on OpenRouter, open-weight models reached ~1/3 of routed token volume by late 2025 and rose through mid-2026. But routers exclude first-party traffic — Google alone disclosed 3.2 quadrillion tokens/month by May 2026, roughly 25× OpenRouter's entire throughput. Corrected for first-party volume, the defensible whole-market open-weight share as of mid-2026 is in the low double digits. Currently false, which is what makes it a prediction.

Baseline: Amazon shortened servers from six years to five, effective January 2025, citing AI and reducing 2025 operating income by about $0.7B. Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle most recently extended. One mover exists, four are extenders, and no company reports accelerators as a segmented asset class.

Baseline: AWS stated in January 2026 that it has never retired an A100 server and remains sold out of them. Google reports full utilization on seven- and eight-year-old TPUs. Public used-GPU transaction data records sales, not utilization. A compute-index administrator reports A100 occupancy averaging about 80 percent over a five-year term window, but no public cohort-level utilization series exists as of mid-2026. The prediction remains unscorable as written.
